## Learnings (added by sessions)

*These rows are the methodology's own framework learnings, recorded as the canonical repo dogfoods itself — canonical sessions append new rows here (append only; do not edit existing rows). Adopter projects do NOT edit this synced table — record project learnings in `CLAUDE.md` → Project-Specific Methodology Adaptations → Project-specific Learnings instead (see 3C).*

| # | Learning | Source | When to Apply |
|---|----------|--------|---------------|
| 1 | Plan-mode output is a draft, not a verified plan. When a prompt contains a multi-phase plan with "implement," the deliverable is a plan document with evidence-based inventory, not Phase 1 code. The gap: Phase 1's task mapping had no entry for plan-mode handoffs, so the session defaulted to "implement." Structural fix: new mapping row + FM #19. | FM #19 discovery | When a prompt contains a multi-phase plan with "implement" — recognize this as a planning workstream. |
| 2 | **Protocol discipline is perishable.** 14 consecutive clean sessions can collapse to 1/10 deliveries within 12 hours of relaxed discipline. The protocol is perishable — it doesn't maintain itself. Each session must actively re-internalize it, not assume it's "already known." The compounding loop works only when every link in the chain is complete. | Field observation | Whenever you catch yourself thinking "I know the protocol, I don't need to re-read it" — re-read it. The fast-collapse case (FM #17 slow-drip's sibling) is real. |
| 3 | Plans should flag "here be dragons" areas where implementation is non-obvious — not all phases are equally risky. Call out which phases need extra caution, what assumptions are load-bearing, and where the executor should stop and re-orient. | Field observation | When writing any multi-phase plan. A plan that presents all phases as equally tractable lies to the executor about where the cost actually lives. |
| 4 | **Verify a plan's output against its completion criteria — not against session duration or count.** Execution speed is not evidence of plan quality, and "fits in one session" is not a planning goal. A plan whose phases each fit cleanly in one session and produce work that matches the completion criteria is high-quality; a plan that tempts the executor to bundle phases or skip close-out to "finish faster" is not. The "1 and done" rule does not bend for high-quality plans. | Field observation (refined from rmsharp feedback on issue #7) | When evaluating a plan or judging plan quality. Resist the temptation to read execution speed as plan quality — they are uncorrelated when the protocol holds. |
| 5 | Code review is a distinct deliverable, not overhead. Reviews that produce actionable plans (exact code snippets, line numbers, implementation order) have higher ROI than vague "this needs improvement" feedback. A review that doesn't identify specific changes a future session can execute is incomplete. | Field observation | When the session deliverable is a code review. Output an actionable plan, not a critique. |
| 6 | A plan written from memory of a file read is an assumption-level claim. Reading implementations before estimating complexity catches wrong assumptions early — estimating from a backlog description alone is unreliable. This is a special case of FM #11 (gaps from memory) and FM #20 (edit from memory) applied to planning. | Field observation | Before estimating effort or scope for any phase, read the actual implementation file. The backlog description is a hint, not a spec. |
| 7 | **Cross-reference completeness at self-review.** When a change adds a citation, an index entry, a glossary term, or any cross-reference between files — and especially when it modifies a numbered set (FMs, principles, phases, anti-patterns, learnings) — `git diff` confirms only the present-side edit; the defect is the *absence* on the destination side, which the diff cannot surface. Grep each cited destination to confirm the citation resolves, and grep nearby prose for set-size or named-membership assertions ("N failure modes", "the three workstreams") that may have drifted. Bidirectional: a new index entry needs its destination to cite back; a grown numbered set needs its size claims re-counted. | Three v2.6 instances: stale "24 failure modes" count, understated `/diagnose` + `/grill-with-docs` citation rows, aspirational `/init` citation (issue #19) | When a change touches any cross-file citation, index, glossary term, or numbered set. At self-review, grep destinations and size claims before committing — do not rely on `git diff` alone. |

---

The user can paste any of these to start a session reliably. The session runner handles the rest — the user does not need to include methodology instructions, close-out instructions, or stop conditions.

**Design:**

**Continuation:**

117	- "This value is always positive" — verify with test data and code analysis
118	- "This test covers the case I'm fixing" — verify by reading the test

121	---
122	
123	## Phase 3: Create (Development-Specific)
124	
125	### The Implementation Plan
126	
127	Before writing code, write a plan:
128	
129	```markdown
130	## What I'm Changing
131	- [File]: [Specific function/method] — [What changes and why]
132	- [File]: [Specific function/method] — [What changes and why]
133	
134	## What I'm NOT Changing (Scope Boundary)
135	- [File]: [Why it's out of scope despite being related]
136

138	- [New test]: [What it verifies]
139	- [Modified test]: [What changes and why]
140	- [Existing test to re-run]: [Why it matters]
141

144

147	2. New tests pass (new behavior verified)

152	
153	For bug fixes, trace to the root cause before implementing:
154	
155	| Level | Question | Example |
156	|-------|----------|---------|
157	| Symptom | What does the user see? | "Button doesn't respond" |
158	| Proximate cause | What code produces the symptom? | Event handler isn't bound |
159	| Root cause | Why is the code wrong? | Handler was removed during refactoring |
160	| Structural cause | What allowed this to happen? | No test covered the click behavior |
161	
162	Fix at the root cause level. Fix at the structural level if practical (add the test).
163	
164	### One Fix, One Commit
165	
166	Each fix or feature should be a single, atomic commit. If a change touches more than one concern, split it into separate commits. This makes rollback possible and review meaningful.
167	
168	---

171	
172	For bug fix campaigns, the "present" step may be lightweight:
173	- Share the implementation plan (not just "I'll fix it")
174	- Highlight any risks or scope concerns
175	- Get approval for any changes that affect shared code or interfaces
176	
177	For feature implementation, present the full plan including test strategy.
178

180	
181	## Scope Validation Questions (Development-Specific)
182	
183	1. Am I fixing the root cause or the symptom?
184	2. Does this change have side effects beyond the intended fix?
185	3. Is the scope of this change proportional to the problem? (A one-line bug shouldn't require a 500-line refactoring)
186	4. Are there other instances of the same bug/pattern that should be fixed in this session?
187	5. Am I changing behavior or just fixing what was always intended?
188	
189	---
190	
191	## Verification Checklist (Development-Specific)
192	
193	Before committing:
194	
195	- [ ] All existing tests pass (no regressions introduced)
196	- [ ] New tests cover the changed behavior
197	- [ ] The fix addresses the root cause, not just the symptom
198	- [ ] The change set matches the implementation plan (no scope creep)
199	- [ ] Code compiles/builds cleanly
200	- [ ] **Runtime verification: the application was actually run and the change was verified visually/functionally.** Compilation is not verification. TypeScript passing is not verification. You must open the application and confirm the behavior. This is a hard gate, not a suggestion. (Session 50 shipped broken code — naturalHeight=0 on reload, passive+preventDefault conflict, wrong nesting order — because it never ran the app. All three bugs would have been caught by opening it once.)
201	- [ ] Adjacent code that shares state or interfaces still works
202	- [ ] The commit message describes WHY, not just WHAT
203	
204	---
205	
206	## Reference Table Formats (Development)
207	
208	### Bug Campaign Tracker
209	| # | Bug | Root Cause | Fix | Tests Added | Status | Session |
210	|---|-----|-----------|-----|-------------|--------|---------|
211	
212	### Regression Log
213	| Session | Change Made | Regression Caused | Root Cause | Prevention |
214	|---------|------------|-------------------|-----------|------------|
215	
216	### Code Health Metrics
217	| File | Test Coverage | Complexity | Last Touched | Known Issues |
218	|------|-------------|------------|-------------|-------------|
219	
220	---
221	
222	## Common Anti-Patterns (Development)
223	
224	1. **Fix-and-forget** — Fixing the symptom without tracing to root cause. The bug will recur in a different form.
225	2. **Scope creep during implementation** — "While I'm here, I'll also refactor this..." Stop. That's a separate session. Commit what you have, then start a new work item.
226	3. **Test-last** — Writing the fix first, then trying to write a test. Write the failing test first — it proves the bug exists and proves the fix works.
227	4. **Assumption-based impact analysis** — "This change only affects X." Verify with grep, not assumptions. The most dangerous regressions come from changes you were SURE were isolated.
228	5. **Compounding errors** — Making a fix, finding it doesn't work, making another fix on top, finding THAT doesn't work. After 2 failed attempts, STOP. Return to Phase 2 (Research). Re-read the code. The mental model is wrong.
229	6. **Big-batch commits** — Combining multiple fixes into one commit because they're "related." Each fix should be independently revertible. One fix, one commit.
230	7. **Skipping the safety commit** — Not creating a rollback point before starting implementation. When things go wrong (and they will), you need a known-good state to return to.
231	8. **Refactoring without a verification baseline** — Extracting, renaming, or restructuring code without capturing pre/post behavior. Handler extraction from a monolith broke memory channels and FM panel because no one verified all handlers after extraction — only the one being worked on. Audit ALL affected code paths, not just the one that's visibly broken. Point-fixing refactoring damage causes cascading regressions.
232	9. **Speed as quality signal** — Finishing implementation faster than expected and treating that as evidence the work is good. Fast completion means verify harder, not celebrate sooner. If a plan collapses multi-session work into one session, spend the saved time on runtime verification.
233	
234	---

237	
238	```
239	Session 4: Handler Extraction Bug Campaign (Session 4 of 6)
240	
241	Pre-Flight: Read SESSION_NOTES.md. Sessions 1-3 extracted 8 handlers from
242	            CatWebSocket.java. Session 3 found 2 regressions in FM panel.
243	            Git status: clean. Build passes. Spot-checked 3 handlers — healthy.
244	
245	Research:   Session 3 regressions: (1) refreshStateFromRadio() only reads
246	            freq+mode, so tone/duplex state is stale after FM operations.
247	            (2) FM handler sends responses before state update completes.
248	            Read CatWebSocket.java handler dispatch. Read FmHandler.java.
249	            Read refreshStateFromRadio() — confirmed it only polls FA/FB/MD.
250	
251	            Prior sessions: Pattern "handler must refresh relevant state after
252	            radio operations." Anti-pattern #3: "Don't assume refreshState
253	            covers all state — it only covers what it explicitly polls."
254	
255	Create:     Plan: Add tone/duplex polling to FmHandler post-operation refresh.
256	            NOT modifying refreshStateFromRadio() (that's a broader change, out of scope).
257	            Files: FmHandler.java (modify), FmHandlerTest.java (add 2 tests).
258	            Risk: Polling tone immediately after set may race with radio firmware.
259	            Mitigation: 50ms delay before tone read (matches existing pattern in BasicControlHandler).
260	
261	Present:    Plan approved. User confirmed FM panel is the priority.
262	
263	Implement:  Safety commit. Added tone polling to FmHandler.
264	            Added 2 tests: tone-after-set, duplex-after-set.
265	            Build passes. FM panel tested manually — tone updates correctly.
266	
267	Close:      0 regressions. Root cause confirmed (stale state after handler
268	            extraction). Pattern: "Extracted handlers must explicitly refresh
269	            the state they affect." Campaign tracker: 4 of 6 handlers fixed.
270	            Recommendation: Session 5 should audit ALL handlers for the same
271	            stale-state pattern, not just the ones with reported bugs.
272	```

## Verification Checklist (Development-Specific)

Before committing:

- [ ] All existing tests pass (no regressions introduced)
- [ ] New tests cover the changed behavior
- [ ] The fix addresses the root cause, not just the symptom
- [ ] The change set matches the implementation plan (no scope creep)
- [ ] Code compiles/builds cleanly
- [ ] **Runtime verification: the application was actually run and the change was verified visually/functionally.** Compilation is not verification. TypeScript passing is not verification. You must open the application and confirm the behavior. This is a hard gate, not a suggestion. (Session 50 shipped broken code — naturalHeight=0 on reload, passive+preventDefault conflict, wrong nesting order — because it never ran the app. All three bugs would have been caught by opening it once.)
- [ ] Adjacent code that shares state or interfaces still works
- [ ] The commit message describes WHY, not just WHAT

---

## Reference Table Formats (Development)

### Bug Campaign Tracker
| # | Bug | Root Cause | Fix | Tests Added | Status | Session |
|---|-----|-----------|-----|-------------|--------|---------|

### Regression Log
| Session | Change Made | Regression Caused | Root Cause | Prevention |
|---------|------------|-------------------|-----------|------------|

### Code Health Metrics
| File | Test Coverage | Complexity | Last Touched | Known Issues |
|------|-------------|------------|-------------|-------------|

---

## Common Anti-Patterns (Development)

1. **Fix-and-forget** — Fixing the symptom without tracing to root cause. The bug will recur in a different form.
2. **Scope creep during implementation** — "While I'm here, I'll also refactor this..." Stop. That's a separate session. Commit what you have, then start a new work item.
3. **Test-last** — Writing the fix first, then trying to write a test. Write the failing test first — it proves the bug exists and proves the fix works.
4. **Assumption-based impact analysis** — "This change only affects X." Verify with grep, not assumptions. The most dangerous regressions come from changes you were SURE were isolated.
5. **Compounding errors** — Making a fix, finding it doesn't work, making another fix on top, finding THAT doesn't work. After 2 failed attempts, STOP. Return to Phase 2 (Research). Re-read the code. The mental model is wrong.
6. **Big-batch commits** — Combining multiple fixes into one commit because they're "related." Each fix should be independently revertible. One fix, one commit.
7. **Skipping the safety commit** — Not creating a rollback point before starting implementation. When things go wrong (and they will), you need a known-good state to return to.
8. **Refactoring without a verification baseline** — Extracting, renaming, or restructuring code without capturing pre/post behavior. Handler extraction from a monolith broke memory channels and FM panel because no one verified all handlers after extraction — only the one being worked on. Audit ALL affected code paths, not just the one that's visibly broken. Point-fixing refactoring damage causes cascading regressions.
9. **Speed as quality signal** — Finishing implementation faster than expected and treating that as evidence the work is good. Fast completion means verify harder, not celebrate sooner. If a plan collapses multi-session work into one session, spend the saved time on runtime verification.

---

## Example Session Outline

```
Session 4: Handler Extraction Bug Campaign (Session 4 of 6)

Pre-Flight: Read SESSION_NOTES.md. Sessions 1-3 extracted 8 handlers from
            CatWebSocket.java. Session 3 found 2 regressions in FM panel.
            Git status: clean. Build passes. Spot-checked 3 handlers — healthy.

Research:   Session 3 regressions: (1) refreshStateFromRadio() only reads
            freq+mode, so tone/duplex state is stale after FM operations.
            (2) FM handler sends responses before state update completes.
            Read CatWebSocket.java handler dispatch. Read FmHandler.java.
            Read refreshStateFromRadio() — confirmed it only polls FA/FB/MD.

            Prior sessions: Pattern "handler must refresh relevant state after
            radio operations." Anti-pattern #3: "Don't assume refreshState
            covers all state — it only covers what it explicitly polls."

Create:     Plan: Add tone/duplex polling to FmHandler post-operation refresh.
            NOT modifying refreshStateFromRadio() (that's a broader change, out of scope).
            Files: FmHandler.java (modify), FmHandlerTest.java (add 2 tests).
            Risk: Polling tone immediately after set may race with radio firmware.
            Mitigation: 50ms delay before tone read (matches existing pattern in BasicControlHandler).

Present:    Plan approved. User confirmed FM panel is the priority.

Implement:  Safety commit. Added tone polling to FmHandler.
            Added 2 tests: tone-after-set, duplex-after-set.
            Build passes. FM panel tested manually — tone updates correctly.

Close:      0 regressions. Root cause confirmed (stale state after handler
            extraction). Pattern: "Extracted handlers must explicitly refresh
            the state they affect." Campaign tracker: 4 of 6 handlers fixed.
            Recommendation: Session 5 should audit ALL handlers for the same
            stale-state pattern, not just the ones with reported bugs.
```

## Copyright(c) 2017-2026 R. Mark Sharp
## This file is part of nprcgenekeepr

# Age-Sex Pyramid Shiny Module

#' Age-Sex Pyramid Module - UI Function
#'
#' @param id character vector of length 1. Module namespace identifier.
#'
#' @return A \code{div} containing age-sex pyramid UI.
#'
#' @seealso \code{\link{modPyramidServer}}
#' @importFrom shiny NS div h3 fluidRow column wellPanel selectInput
#' @importFrom shiny numericInput hr checkboxInput downloadButton tabsetPanel
#' @importFrom shiny tabPanel plotOutput tableOutput includeHTML sliderInput
#' @importFrom shiny uiOutput helpText
#' @family Shiny modules
#' @export
modPyramidUI <- function(id) {
  ns <- NS(id)

  div(
    id = ns("moduleContainer"),
    `data-ready` = "false",
    `data-module` = "pyramid",

    h3("Age-Sex Pyramid Analysis"),
    fluidRow(
      column(3L,
             wellPanel(
               selectInput(ns("ageUnit"), "Age Unit:",
                           choices = c(Years = "years", Months = "months")),
               numericInput(ns("ageBin"), "Bin Size:", value = 2L, min = 1L,
                            max = 10L),
               selectInput(ns("colorScheme"), "Color Scheme:",
                           choices = c(Default = "default",
                                       Viridis = "viridis")),
               hr(),
               checkboxInput(ns("showCounts"), "Show counts", TRUE),
               hr(),
               sliderInput(ns("plotHeight"), "Plot Height (pixels):",
                           min = 400L, max = 1500L, value = 600L, step = 50L),
               helpText(
                 "Increase height for better visibility with many age groups",
                        style =
                   "font-size: 14px; color: darblue; font-weight: bold;"),
               hr(),
               sliderInput(ns("ageLabelSize"), "Age Label Size:",
                           min = 0.5, max = 2.0, value = 1.0, step = 0.1),
               hr(),
               downloadButton(ns("downloadPlot"), "Download Plot")
             ),
             div(
               style = paste(
                 "padding: 10px; border: 1px solid lightgray;",
                 "background-color: #EDEDED; border-radius: 25px;",
                 "box-shadow: 0 0 5px 2px #888; margin-top: 10px;"
               ),
               includeHTML(
                 system.file("extdata", "ui_guidance", "pyramidPlot.html",
                             package = "nprcgenekeepr")
               )
             )
      ),
      column(9L,
             tabsetPanel(
               tabPanel("Plot", uiOutput(ns("pyramidPlotUI"))),
               tabPanel("Statistics", tableOutput(ns("pyramidStats")))
             )
      )
    )
  )
}

#' Age-Sex Pyramid Module - Server Function
#'
#' @param id character vector of length 1. Module namespace identifier.
#' @param pedigreeData reactive returning pedigree data frame.
#'
#' @return A list with two elements: \code{pedigree}, a reactive
#'   returning the pedigree data frame, and \code{animalCount}, a
#'   reactive returning the number of animal rows.
#'
#' @seealso \code{\link{modPyramidUI}}
#' @importFrom grDevices dev.off png
#' @importFrom shiny moduleServer reactive eventReactive renderPlot renderTable
#' @importFrom shiny downloadHandler req isolate tagList renderUI
#' @importFrom graphics text
#' @family Shiny modules
#' @export
modPyramidServer <- function(id, pedigreeData) {
  moduleServer(id, function(input, output, session) {

    ns <- session$ns

    # Dynamic plot container with adjustable height
    output$pyramidPlotUI <- renderUI({
      height <- if (!is.null(input$plotHeight)) input$plotHeight else 600L
      plotOutput(ns("pyramidPlot"), height = paste0(height, "px"))
    })

    # Render pyramid plot with UI controls
    output$pyramidPlot <- renderPlot({
      req(pedigreeData())
      getPyramidPlot(
        ped = pedigreeData(),
        binWidth = input$ageBin,
        ageUnit = input$ageUnit,
        colorScheme = input$colorScheme,
        showCounts = input$showCounts,
        ageLabelCex = input$ageLabelSize
      )
    })

    output$pyramidStats <- renderTable({
      req(pedigreeData())
      ped <- pedigreeData()
      data.frame(
        Metric = c("Total", "Males", "Females"),
        Value = c(nrow(ped),
                  sum(ped$sex == "M", na.rm = TRUE),
                  sum(ped$sex == "F", na.rm = TRUE)),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    })

    # Signal data-ready when pyramid is rendered (for E2E testing)
    observe({
      req(pedigreeData())
      session$sendCustomMessage("setDataReady", list(
        selector = paste0("#", session$ns("moduleContainer")),
        ready = TRUE
      ))
    })

    output$downloadPlot <- downloadHandler(
      filename = function() paste0("pyramid_", Sys.Date(), ".png"),
      content = function(file) {
        # Scale PNG dimensions based on user's plot height selection
        plotHeight <- if (!is.null(input$plotHeight)) input$plotHeight else 600L
        # Maintain aspect ratio: width = height * 1.5
        png(file, width = as.integer(plotHeight * 1.5), height = plotHeight)
        getPyramidPlot(
          ped = pedigreeData(),
          binWidth = input$ageBin,
          ageUnit = input$ageUnit,
          colorScheme = input$colorScheme,
          showCounts = input$showCounts,
          ageLabelCex = input$ageLabelSize
        )
        dev.off()
      }
    )

    list(
      pedigree = reactive(pedigreeData()),
      animalCount = reactive(nrow(pedigreeData()))
    )
  })
}

5	# Issue #13 item-3 follow-up (S220), revised for the issue #95 keep-all revert
6	# (S234): gvaConvergence() must honor outside-information kinship overrides the
7	# SAME way reportGV() does -- apply them to the (proband-filtered) kinship matrix
8	# before mean kinship via the shared prepareKinshipOverrides() helper. The
9	# override REFINES a kinship cell (issue #13); it never suppresses a focal's
10	# +sexMean/2 unknown-parent prior -- every one-unknown animal keeps its
11	# correction (keep-all). gvaConvergence ranks on the same mean-kinship z-scores
12	# reportGV uses; an override that did not reach this pipeline would make the
13	# convergence diagnostic disagree with the report it is meant to characterize.
14	#
15	# Testability note: the override's effect on gvaConvergence's OUTPUT (the
16	# convergence curve) is visible only through gene-drop "churn" near the top-k
17	# boundary. On a no-gu pedigree (qcPed) every half-split agrees (overlap == 1,
18	# rankAgreement == 1) regardless of the mean-kinship order, so the override is
19	# output-invisible there. Therefore the "override reaches the ranking" assertion
20	# uses the gu-bearing convergence fixture; the one-unknown #9 interaction (no
21	# per-animal mean kinship is returned by gvaConvergence) is exercised on qcPed,
22	# and its NUMERIC correctness is covered by construction-parity with reportGV
23	# plus the reportGV D10/D5/keep-all tests in test_reportGV.R, because
24	# gvaConvergence reuses the identical correctUnknownParentMeanKinship() call.
25	
26	# Exact copy of the convergence fixture (see test_gvaConvergence.R), renamed to
27	# avoid a cross-file clash, so this file also runs in isolation. A deterministic
28	# dense-mid-range half-sib web: founders are excluded from the proband
29	# population, the 70 offspring are the probands, and the gene drop is the only
30	# seed consumer, so a fixed seed gives a byte-identical convergence curve.
31	makeConvFixtureOv <- function() {
32	  w <- rep(5L, 14L) # sire window widths (sire fan sizes)
33	  b <- 15L # number of founder dams
34	  a <- length(w)
35	  sids <- sprintf("S%03d", seq_len(a))
36	  dids <- sprintf("D%03d", seq_len(b))
37	  id <- c(sids, dids)
38	  sire <- rep(NA_character_, a + b)
39	  dam <- rep(NA_character_, a + b)
40	  sex <- c(rep("M", a), rep("F", b))
41	  off <- character(0L)
42	  ocount <- 0L
43	  start <- 1L
44	  for (i in seq_len(a)) {
45	    for (j in seq_len(w[i])) {
46	      dj <- ((start + j - 2L) %% b) + 1L
47	      ocount <- ocount + 1L
48	      o <- sprintf("O%04d", ocount)
49	      id <- c(id, o)
50	      sire <- c(sire, sids[i])
51	      dam <- c(dam, dids[dj])
52	      sex <- c(sex, if (ocount %% 2L == 0L) "F" else "M")
53	      off <- c(off, o)
54	    }
55	    start <- start + max(1L, w[i] - 1L) # overlap windows so dam fans vary
56	  }
57	  ped <- data.frame(
58	    id = id, sire = sire, dam = dam, sex = sex,
59	    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
60	  )
61	  ped$gen <- findGeneration(ped$id, ped$sire, ped$dam)
62	  list(ped = ped, pop = off)
63	}
64	
65	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
66	# (1) D10 regression: a NULL or zero-row override leaves the convergence result
67	# byte-identical to the no-override run -- the default code path is untouched.
68	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
69	test_that("gvaConvergence with NULL or zero-row overrides equals the no-override run", {
70	  fx <- makeConvFixtureOv()
71	  base <- gvaConvergence(fx$ped, pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L)
72	
73	  nullOv <- gvaConvergence(fx$ped,
74	    pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L,
75	    kinshipOverrides = NULL
76	  )
77	  expect_equal(nullOv$convergence, base$convergence)
78	  expect_identical(nullOv$recommendedIter, base$recommendedIter)
79	
80	  zero <- data.frame(
81	    id1 = character(0), id2 = character(0), kinship = numeric(0),
82	    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
83	  )
84	  zeroOv <- gvaConvergence(fx$ped,
85	    pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L,
86	    kinshipOverrides = zero
87	  )
88	  expect_equal(zeroOv$convergence, base$convergence)
89	})
90	
91	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
92	# (2) An override that shifts mean-kinship z-scores reaches the ranking pipeline
93	# and changes the convergence curve; the change is deterministic under a fixed
94	# seed. The override is five offspring pairs at near-max kinship (0.49), chosen
95	# so the perturbation is robust (verified to move the curve at this nMax/seed).
96	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
97	test_that("gvaConvergence applies kinship overrides to the ranking (deterministic)", {
98	  fx <- makeConvFixtureOv()
99	  off <- fx$pop
100	  ov <- data.frame(
101	    id1 = off[c(1, 3, 5, 7, 9)],
102	    id2 = off[c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10)],
103	    kinship = 0.49,
104	    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
105	  )
106	  base <- gvaConvergence(fx$ped, pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L)
107	  over <- suppressMessages(gvaConvergence(fx$ped,
108	    pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L, kinshipOverrides = ov
109	  ))
110	
111	  # the override reaches the ranking: the convergence curve is NOT identical
112	  expect_false(isTRUE(all.equal(base$convergence, over$convergence)))
113	
114	  # deterministic under a fixed seed: a second identical run matches the first
115	  over2 <- suppressMessages(gvaConvergence(fx$ped,
116	    pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L, kinshipOverrides = ov
117	  ))
118	  expect_equal(over$convergence, over2$convergence)
119	})
120	
121	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
122	# (3) D5 soft warn-drop: an override row referencing an id outside the proband
123	# set warns and the run completes -- the strict applyKinshipOverrides leaf never
124	# aborts the diagnostic. With only an out-of-set row, the result equals baseline.
125	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
126	test_that("gvaConvergence warn-drops an out-of-set override id without aborting", {
127	  fx <- makeConvFixtureOv()
128	  # founders (e.g. S001) are excluded from the proband population
129	  expect_false("S001" %in% fx$pop)
130

132	    id1 = fx$pop[1], id2 = "S001", kinship = 0.1,
133	    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
134	  )
135	  base <- gvaConvergence(fx$ped, pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L)
136	  expect_warning(
137	    res <- gvaConvergence(fx$ped,
138	      pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L, kinshipOverrides = badOv
139	    ),
140	    "not in the analysis set"
141	  )
142	  expect_equal(res$convergence, base$convergence)
143	})
144	
145	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
146	# (4) Strict validation propagates: an override above the positive-semidefinite
147	# bound sqrt(self-kinship product) stops -- applyKinshipOverrides is the strict
148	# leaf and gvaConvergence must not swallow that error.
149	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
150	test_that("gvaConvergence errors on an override above the PSD bound", {
151	  fx <- makeConvFixtureOv()
152	  # an offspring pair's self-kinship is ~0.5, so the bound is ~0.5; 0.9 exceeds it
153	  badVal <- data.frame(
154	    id1 = fx$pop[1], id2 = fx$pop[2], kinship = 0.9,
155	    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
156	  )
157	  expect_error(
158	    suppressMessages(gvaConvergence(fx$ped,
159	      pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L, kinshipOverrides = badVal
160	    )),
161	    "above the maximum"
162	  )
163	})

167	# one-unknown-parent rankable animal runs clean and is honored (the
168	# "N kinship override(s) applied." message fires). On qcPed the convergence

172	# gvaConvergence reuses the identical correctUnknownParentMeanKinship() call and
173	# returns no per-animal mean kinship of its own.
174	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Issue #13 item-3 follow-up (S220), revised for the issue #95 keep-all revert
# (S234): gvaConvergence() must honor outside-information kinship overrides the
# SAME way reportGV() does -- apply them to the (proband-filtered) kinship matrix
# before mean kinship via the shared prepareKinshipOverrides() helper. The
# override REFINES a kinship cell (issue #13); it never suppresses a focal's
# +sexMean/2 unknown-parent prior -- every one-unknown animal keeps its
# correction (keep-all). gvaConvergence ranks on the same mean-kinship z-scores
# reportGV uses; an override that did not reach this pipeline would make the
# convergence diagnostic disagree with the report it is meant to characterize.
#
# Testability note: the override's effect on gvaConvergence's OUTPUT (the
# convergence curve) is visible only through gene-drop "churn" near the top-k
# boundary. On a no-gu pedigree (qcPed) every half-split agrees (overlap == 1,
# rankAgreement == 1) regardless of the mean-kinship order, so the override is
# output-invisible there. Therefore the "override reaches the ranking" assertion
# uses the gu-bearing convergence fixture; the one-unknown #9 interaction (no
# per-animal mean kinship is returned by gvaConvergence) is exercised on qcPed,
# and its NUMERIC correctness is covered by construction-parity with reportGV
# plus the reportGV D10/D5/keep-all tests in test_reportGV.R, because
# gvaConvergence reuses the identical correctUnknownParentMeanKinship() call.

# Exact copy of the convergence fixture (see test_gvaConvergence.R), renamed to
# avoid a cross-file clash, so this file also runs in isolation. A deterministic
# dense-mid-range half-sib web: founders are excluded from the proband
# population, the 70 offspring are the probands, and the gene drop is the only
# seed consumer, so a fixed seed gives a byte-identical convergence curve.
makeConvFixtureOv <- function() {
  w <- rep(5L, 14L) # sire window widths (sire fan sizes)
  b <- 15L # number of founder dams
  a <- length(w)
  sids <- sprintf("S%03d", seq_len(a))
  dids <- sprintf("D%03d", seq_len(b))
  id <- c(sids, dids)
  sire <- rep(NA_character_, a + b)
  dam <- rep(NA_character_, a + b)
  sex <- c(rep("M", a), rep("F", b))
  off <- character(0L)
  ocount <- 0L
  start <- 1L
  for (i in seq_len(a)) {
    for (j in seq_len(w[i])) {
      dj <- ((start + j - 2L) %% b) + 1L
      ocount <- ocount + 1L
      o <- sprintf("O%04d", ocount)
      id <- c(id, o)
      sire <- c(sire, sids[i])
      dam <- c(dam, dids[dj])
      sex <- c(sex, if (ocount %% 2L == 0L) "F" else "M")
      off <- c(off, o)
    }
    start <- start + max(1L, w[i] - 1L) # overlap windows so dam fans vary
  }
  ped <- data.frame(
    id = id, sire = sire, dam = dam, sex = sex,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  ped$gen <- findGeneration(ped$id, ped$sire, ped$dam)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# (1) D10 regression: a NULL or zero-row override leaves the convergence result
# byte-identical to the no-override run -- the default code path is untouched.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
test_that("gvaConvergence with NULL or zero-row overrides equals the no-override run", {
  fx <- makeConvFixtureOv()
  base <- gvaConvergence(fx$ped, pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L)

  nullOv <- gvaConvergence(fx$ped,
    pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L,
    kinshipOverrides = NULL
  )
  expect_equal(nullOv$convergence, base$convergence)
  expect_identical(nullOv$recommendedIter, base$recommendedIter)

  zero <- data.frame(
    id1 = character(0), id2 = character(0), kinship = numeric(0),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  zeroOv <- gvaConvergence(fx$ped,
    pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L,
    kinshipOverrides = zero
  )
  expect_equal(zeroOv$convergence, base$convergence)
})

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# (2) An override that shifts mean-kinship z-scores reaches the ranking pipeline
# and changes the convergence curve; the change is deterministic under a fixed
# seed. The override is five offspring pairs at near-max kinship (0.49), chosen
# so the perturbation is robust (verified to move the curve at this nMax/seed).
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
test_that("gvaConvergence applies kinship overrides to the ranking (deterministic)", {
  fx <- makeConvFixtureOv()
  off <- fx$pop
  ov <- data.frame(
    id1 = off[c(1, 3, 5, 7, 9)],
    id2 = off[c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10)],
    kinship = 0.49,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  base <- gvaConvergence(fx$ped, pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L)
  over <- suppressMessages(gvaConvergence(fx$ped,
    pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L, kinshipOverrides = ov
  ))

  # the override reaches the ranking: the convergence curve is NOT identical
  expect_false(isTRUE(all.equal(base$convergence, over$convergence)))

  # deterministic under a fixed seed: a second identical run matches the first
  over2 <- suppressMessages(gvaConvergence(fx$ped,
    pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L, kinshipOverrides = ov
  ))
  expect_equal(over$convergence, over2$convergence)
})

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# (3) D5 soft warn-drop: an override row referencing an id outside the proband
# set warns and the run completes -- the strict applyKinshipOverrides leaf never
# aborts the diagnostic. With only an out-of-set row, the result equals baseline.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
test_that("gvaConvergence warn-drops an out-of-set override id without aborting", {
  fx <- makeConvFixtureOv()
  # founders (e.g. S001) are excluded from the proband population
  expect_false("S001" %in% fx$pop)

  badOv <- data.frame(
    id1 = fx$pop[1], id2 = "S001", kinship = 0.1,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  base <- gvaConvergence(fx$ped, pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L)
  expect_warning(
    res <- gvaConvergence(fx$ped,
      pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L, kinshipOverrides = badOv
    ),
    "not in the analysis set"
  )
  expect_equal(res$convergence, base$convergence)
})

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# (4) Strict validation propagates: an override above the positive-semidefinite
# bound sqrt(self-kinship product) stops -- applyKinshipOverrides is the strict
# leaf and gvaConvergence must not swallow that error.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
test_that("gvaConvergence errors on an override above the PSD bound", {
  fx <- makeConvFixtureOv()
  # an offspring pair's self-kinship is ~0.5, so the bound is ~0.5; 0.9 exceeds it
  badVal <- data.frame(
    id1 = fx$pop[1], id2 = fx$pop[2], kinship = 0.9,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  expect_error(
    suppressMessages(gvaConvergence(fx$ped,
      pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L, kinshipOverrides = badVal
    )),
    "above the maximum"
  )
})

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# (5) reportGV fidelity -- the keep-all / issue-#9 path: an override on a real
# one-unknown-parent rankable animal runs clean and is honored (the
# "N kinship override(s) applied." message fires). On qcPed the convergence
# metrics are gu-free (always 1.0), so the override cannot change the OUTPUT
# curve there; the keep-all NUMERIC is covered by reportGV's tests
# (test_reportGV.R) and test_correctUnknownParentMeanKinship.R, since
# gvaConvergence reuses the identical correctUnknownParentMeanKinship() call and
# returns no per-animal mean kinship of its own.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
test_that("gvaConvergence honors an override on a one-unknown-parent animal", {
  ped <- nprcgenekeepr::qcPed
  X <- "0K7VJN" # male, one-unknown (sire missing) -- see test_reportGV.R
  Y <- "N2XF08" # known parentage
  isU <- function(x) is.na(x) | nprcgenekeepr:::isGeneratedUnknownId(x)
  # fixture guards: fail loudly if qcPed changes instead of mis-testing
  expect_true(all(c(X, Y) %in% as.character(ped$id)))
  expect_true(xor(isU(ped$sire[ped$id == X]), isU(ped$dam[ped$id == X])))

  ov <- data.frame(id1 = X, id2 = Y, kinship = 0.25, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  res <- NULL
  expect_message(
    res <- gvaConvergence(ped,
      nMax = 200L, grid = c(25L, 50L, 100L), seed = 1L, kinshipOverrides = ov
    ),
    "kinship override"
  )
  expect_s3_class(res, "nprcgenekeeprGVConv")

  # qcPed is gu-free -> the override cannot change the (always-1.0) curve; it
  # must still converge at the grid floor exactly as the no-override run does
  base <- gvaConvergence(ped, nMax = 200L, grid = c(25L, 50L, 100L), seed = 1L)
  expect_equal(res$convergence, base$convergence)
})

#' Create an age-sex pyramid plot of a pedigree
#'

#'
#' @inheritParams reportGV
#' @param binWidth numeric bin width for age groups (default 2).
#' @param ageUnit character either "years" (default) or "months".
#' @param colorScheme character color scheme: "default" (blue/pink) or
#'   "viridis" (colorblind-friendly).

#' @importFrom lubridate now

#' @export
#' @examples
#' library(nprcgenekeepr)

#' getPyramidPlot(qcPed, binWidth = 5, colorScheme = "viridis")
getPyramidPlot <- function(ped = NULL, binWidth = 2L, ageUnit = "years",
                           colorScheme = "default", showCounts = TRUE,
                           ageLabelCex = 1.0) {
  if (is.null(ped)) {
    ped <- getPyramidAgeDist()
  }


  # Convert age to months if requested
  if (ageUnit == "months" && "age" %in% names(ped)) {
    ped$age <- ped$age * 12.0
  }

  opar <- par(no.readonly = TRUE) # nolint: undesirable_function_linter
  on.exit(par(opar)) # nolint: undesirable_function_linter
  par(bg = "#FFF8DC") # nolint: undesirable_function_linter

  # Ensure binWidth is at least 1

binWidth <- max(1L, as.integer(binWidth))

  axModulas <- 5L
  maxAge <- getPedMaxAge(ped)

  # Handle case where maxAge might be very small or zero
  if (is.na(maxAge) || maxAge < binWidth) {
    maxAge <- binWidth
  }

  upperAges <- seq(
    binWidth,
    makeRoundUp(maxAge, binWidth), binWidth
  )
  lowerAges <- upperAges - binWidth

  bins <- fillBins(ped, lowerAges, upperAges)
  maxAx <- max(getMaxAx(bins, axModulas))

  # Create age labels with appropriate unit
  ageUnitLabel <- if (ageUnit == "months") "mo" else "yr"
  ageLabels <- stri_c(lowerAges, "-", upperAges - 1L)

    fcol <- color.gradient(0.741, 0.639, 0.173)  # viridis yellow-ish

    mcol <- color.gradient(0L, 0L, 0.5)
    fcol <- color.gradient(1L, 0.5, 0.5)
  }

  currentDate <- now()
  axBy <- maxAx / axModulas
  axGap <- axBy * 0.6
  gap <- axGap
  laxlab <- seq(0L, maxAx, by = axBy)
  raxlab <- seq(0L, maxAx, by = axBy)

  # Call pyramid.plot directly with additional parameters
  pyramid.plot(
    lx = bins$males,
    rx = bins$females,
    labels = ageLabels,
    main = stri_c(
      "Total on ",
      lubridate::year(currentDate),
      "-",
      lubridate::month(currentDate, label = TRUE),
      "-",
      lubridate::day(currentDate),
      ": ",
      sum(c(bins$males, bins$females))
    ),
    top.labels = c(
      stri_c("Male = ", sum(bins$males)),
      paste0("Age (", ageUnitLabel, ")"),
      stri_c("Female = ", sum(bins$females))
    ),
    lxcol = mcol,
    rxcol = fcol,
    laxlab = laxlab,
    raxlab = raxlab,
    gap = gap,
    unit = "Number of Animals",
    show.values = showCounts,
    ndig = 0L,
    labelcex = ageLabelCex
  )
}

#' @param overrides data.frame of overrides (\code{id1}, \code{id2},
#' \code{kinship}); \code{NULL} or a zero-row frame is a no-op returning
#' \code{kmat} unchanged. Validated with \code{\link{checkKinshipOverrides}}.
#' @return \code{kmat} with the override cells replaced (symmetric).
#' @export
#' @examples
#' ped <- nprcgenekeepr::qcPed
#' kmat <- kinship(ped$id, ped$sire, ped$dam, ped$gen)
#' overrides <- data.frame(
#'   id1 = ped$id[1], id2 = ped$id[2], kinship = 0.25,
#'   stringsAsFactors = FALSE
#' )
#' kmat <- applyKinshipOverrides(kmat, overrides)
applyKinshipOverrides <- function(kmat, overrides) {
  if (is.null(overrides) || nrow(overrides) == 0L) {
    return(kmat)
  }
  overrides <- checkKinshipOverrides(overrides)

  ids <- rownames(kmat)
  unknown <- setdiff(unique(c(overrides$id1, overrides$id2)), ids)
  if (length(unknown) > 0L) {
    stop("Kinship override id(s) not found in the matrix: ",
      toString(unknown), ".")
  }

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(overrides))) {
    id1 <- overrides$id1[i]
    id2 <- overrides$id2[i]
    value <- overrides$kinship[i]
    bound <- sqrt(kmat[id1, id1] * kmat[id2, id2])
    if (value > bound) {
      stop(sprintf(
        paste0("Kinship override for (%s, %s) is %g, above the maximum ",
          "%g = sqrt(self-kinship product) for that pair."),
        id1, id2, value, bound

#' prior, which is kept for every one-unknown animal (issue #95 keep-all
#' revert). With no override / an empty frame the result is byte-identical to
#' no override (D10).
#'
#' @param kmat dense, symmetric, id-named proband kinship matrix.
#' @param kinshipOverrides raw user override data.frame (\code{id1}, \code{id2},
#' \code{kinship}), or \code{NULL}.
#' @return list with \code{kmat} (the patched matrix).
#' @noRd
prepareKinshipOverrides <- function(kmat, kinshipOverrides) {
  if (is.null(kinshipOverrides) || nrow(kinshipOverrides) == 0L) {
    return(list(kmat = kmat))
  }
  overrides <- checkKinshipOverrides(kinshipOverrides)
  inMatrix <- overrides$id1 %in% rownames(kmat) &
    overrides$id2 %in% rownames(kmat)
  if (!all(inMatrix)) {
    dropped <- setdiff(
      unique(c(overrides$id1[!inMatrix], overrides$id2[!inMatrix])),
      rownames(kmat)
    )
    warning(sprintf(
      paste0("Dropping %d kinship override row(s) referencing id(s) not in ",
        "the analysis set: %s."),
      sum(!inMatrix), toString(dropped)
    ))
    overrides <- overrides[inMatrix, , drop = FALSE]
  }
  if (nrow(overrides) > 0L) {
    kmat <- applyKinshipOverrides(kmat, overrides)
  }
  list(kmat = kmat)
}

prepareKinshipOverrides <- function(kmat, kinshipOverrides) {

content.text:
**TDD phase: PRE-RED.** No tests or production code have been changed. The only edit so far is the session stub in `SESSION_NOTES.md`.

I reproduced all 7 warnings, and they have two separate causes. `AskUserQuestion` isn't available in this environment, so I'm asking the scope question here in prose instead.

## Findings

**`test_modPyramid.R` has 5 warnings, all from the "handles input changes" test.**
- Each one is `no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf`, raised at `max(ped$age, na.rm = TRUE)` inside `getPedMaxAge()`. `getPyramidPlot()` calls it on every re-render.
- They fire on the `setInputs` calls for `ageUnit` (twice), `ageBin`, `colorScheme` and `ageLabelSize`.
- The test fixtures have a `birth` column but no `age` column. `getPyramidPlot()` documents that it needs `sex` and `age`, so the fixtures break that contract. The sibling file `test_modPyramid_coverage.R` already has a correct fixture, `pyramidTestPed()`, whose comment says it renders "without warning".
- In the app, pedigrees come from `qcStudbook`, which always adds `age`, so normal use doesn't hit this. It does fire for a pedigree with all-NA ages, a zero-row pedigree, or no `age` column. The plot still renders correctly in those cases (`-Inf < binWidth` falls into the existing fallback), but the warning is spurious.

**`test_gvaConvergence_kinshipOverrides.R` has 2 warnings, both from test (4), the 0.9 override.**
- `checkKinshipOverrides` (`R/checkKinshipOverrides.R`) deliberately warns about values above 0.5: "valid only for inbred pairs". The test only asserts the subsequent error.
- The warning fires twice because `prepareKinshipOverrides` validates the overrides, then `applyKinshipOverrides` validates them again. I'm leaving that redundancy alone and will note it for a future session.

I ran all of this with renv bypassed, because the project library isn't restored. I used the user library (`pkgload`, `testthat` and `shiny` are installed), so package versions may differ from `renv.lock`.

## Decision needed

- **Option A, test hygiene only (recommended).**
  - Give the `test_modPyramid.R` fixtures an `age` column, as `pyramidTestPed()` does.
  - In the gvaConvergence test, assert the documented `> 0.5` warning explicitly alongside the error. I'd capture warnings with `withCallingHandlers` rather than nested `expect_warning`, so the test doesn't depend on the warning firing twice.
  - No production code changes. The RED artifact is the warning-count check on those tests.
- **Option B, A plus hardening.**
  - Also make `getPyramidPlot()` (or `getPedMaxAge()`) handle all-NA and empty ages without the spurious `-Inf` warning. The plot's existing `is.na(maxAge)` check shows NA was the intended signal.
  - This needs its own RED tests, and changing exported `getPedMaxAge()` would be a behavior change needing a NEWS entry. Guarding inside `getPyramidPlot()` only would be narrower.

I recommend A because all 7 warnings come from test fixtures and test assertions, not from a production defect, and S313 framed #121 as test hygiene. Say "A" or "B" and I'll declare RED and start writing the failing tests.

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# (4) Strict validation propagates: an override above the positive-semidefinite
# bound sqrt(self-kinship product) stops -- applyKinshipOverrides is the strict
# leaf and gvaConvergence must not swallow that error.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
test_that("gvaConvergence errors on an override above the PSD bound", {
  fx <- makeConvFixtureOv()
  # an offspring pair's self-kinship is ~0.5, so the bound is ~0.5; 0.9 exceeds it
  badVal <- data.frame(
    id1 = fx$pop[1], id2 = fx$pop[2], kinship = 0.9,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  expect_error(
    suppressMessages(gvaConvergence(fx$ped,
      pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L, kinshipOverrides = badVal
    )),
    "above the maximum"
  )
})

# leaf and gvaConvergence must not swallow that error. Issue #121: a value above
# 0.5 also draws checkKinshipOverrides()'s documented "valid only for inbred
# pairs" warning (emitted before the strict per-pair error), so assert it
# rather than leave it unasserted.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
test_that("gvaConvergence errors on an override above the PSD bound", {
  fx <- makeConvFixtureOv()
  # an offspring pair's self-kinship is ~0.5, so the bound is ~0.5; 0.9 exceeds it
  badVal <- data.frame(
    id1 = fx$pop[1], id2 = fx$pop[2], kinship = 0.9,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  expect_warning(
    expect_error(
      suppressMessages(gvaConvergence(fx$ped,
        pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L, kinshipOverrides = badVal
      )),
      "above the maximum"
    ),
    "valid only for inbred pairs"
  )
})

library(testthat)

# Issue #13 item-3 follow-up (S220), revised for the issue #95 keep-all revert
# (S234): gvaConvergence() must honor outside-information kinship overrides the
# SAME way reportGV() does -- apply them to the (proband-filtered) kinship matrix
# before mean kinship via the shared prepareKinshipOverrides() helper. The
# override REFINES a kinship cell (issue #13); it never suppresses a focal's
# +sexMean/2 unknown-parent prior -- every one-unknown animal keeps its
# correction (keep-all). gvaConvergence ranks on the same mean-kinship z-scores
# reportGV uses; an override that did not reach this pipeline would make the
# convergence diagnostic disagree with the report it is meant to characterize.
#
# Testability note: the override's effect on gvaConvergence's OUTPUT (the
# convergence curve) is visible only through gene-drop "churn" near the top-k
# boundary. On a no-gu pedigree (qcPed) every half-split agrees (overlap == 1,
# rankAgreement == 1) regardless of the mean-kinship order, so the override is
# output-invisible there. Therefore the "override reaches the ranking" assertion
# uses the gu-bearing convergence fixture; the one-unknown #9 interaction (no
# per-animal mean kinship is returned by gvaConvergence) is exercised on qcPed,
# and its NUMERIC correctness is covered by construction-parity with reportGV
# plus the reportGV D10/D5/keep-all tests in test_reportGV.R, because
# gvaConvergence reuses the identical correctUnknownParentMeanKinship() call.

# Exact copy of the convergence fixture (see test_gvaConvergence.R), renamed to
# avoid a cross-file clash, so this file also runs in isolation. A deterministic
# dense-mid-range half-sib web: founders are excluded from the proband
# population, the 70 offspring are the probands, and the gene drop is the only
# seed consumer, so a fixed seed gives a byte-identical convergence curve.
makeConvFixtureOv <- function() {
  w <- rep(5L, 14L) # sire window widths (sire fan sizes)
  b <- 15L # number of founder dams
  a <- length(w)
  sids <- sprintf("S%03d", seq_len(a))
  dids <- sprintf("D%03d", seq_len(b))
  id <- c(sids, dids)
  sire <- rep(NA_character_, a + b)
  dam <- rep(NA_character_, a + b)
  sex <- c(rep("M", a), rep("F", b))
  off <- character(0L)
  ocount <- 0L
  start <- 1L
  for (i in seq_len(a)) {
    for (j in seq_len(w[i])) {
      dj <- ((start + j - 2L) %% b) + 1L
      ocount <- ocount + 1L
      o <- sprintf("O%04d", ocount)
      id <- c(id, o)
      sire <- c(sire, sids[i])
      dam <- c(dam, dids[dj])
      sex <- c(sex, if (ocount %% 2L == 0L) "F" else "M")
      off <- c(off, o)
    }
    start <- start + max(1L, w[i] - 1L) # overlap windows so dam fans vary
  }
  ped <- data.frame(
    id = id, sire = sire, dam = dam, sex = sex,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  ped$gen <- findGeneration(ped$id, ped$sire, ped$dam)
  list(ped = ped, pop = off)
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# (1) D10 regression: a NULL or zero-row override leaves the convergence result
# byte-identical to the no-override run -- the default code path is untouched.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
test_that("gvaConvergence with NULL or zero-row overrides equals the no-override run", {
  fx <- makeConvFixtureOv()
  base <- gvaConvergence(fx$ped, pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L)

  nullOv <- gvaConvergence(fx$ped,
    pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L,
    kinshipOverrides = NULL
  )
  expect_equal(nullOv$convergence, base$convergence)
  expect_identical(nullOv$recommendedIter, base$recommendedIter)

  zero <- data.frame(
    id1 = character(0), id2 = character(0), kinship = numeric(0),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  zeroOv <- gvaConvergence(fx$ped,
    pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L,
    kinshipOverrides = zero
  )
  expect_equal(zeroOv$convergence, base$convergence)
})

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# (2) An override that shifts mean-kinship z-scores reaches the ranking pipeline
# and changes the convergence curve; the change is deterministic under a fixed
# seed. The override is five offspring pairs at near-max kinship (0.49), chosen
# so the perturbation is robust (verified to move the curve at this nMax/seed).
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
test_that("gvaConvergence applies kinship overrides to the ranking (deterministic)", {
  fx <- makeConvFixtureOv()
  off <- fx$pop
  ov <- data.frame(
    id1 = off[c(1, 3, 5, 7, 9)],
    id2 = off[c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10)],
    kinship = 0.49,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  base <- gvaConvergence(fx$ped, pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L)
  over <- suppressMessages(gvaConvergence(fx$ped,
    pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L, kinshipOverrides = ov
  ))

  # the override reaches the ranking: the convergence curve is NOT identical
  expect_false(isTRUE(all.equal(base$convergence, over$convergence)))

  # deterministic under a fixed seed: a second identical run matches the first
  over2 <- suppressMessages(gvaConvergence(fx$ped,
    pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L, kinshipOverrides = ov
  ))
  expect_equal(over$convergence, over2$convergence)
})

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# (3) D5 soft warn-drop: an override row referencing an id outside the proband
# set warns and the run completes -- the strict applyKinshipOverrides leaf never
# aborts the diagnostic. With only an out-of-set row, the result equals baseline.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
test_that("gvaConvergence warn-drops an out-of-set override id without aborting", {
  fx <- makeConvFixtureOv()
  # founders (e.g. S001) are excluded from the proband population
  expect_false("S001" %in% fx$pop)

  badOv <- data.frame(
    id1 = fx$pop[1], id2 = "S001", kinship = 0.1,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  base <- gvaConvergence(fx$ped, pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L)
  expect_warning(
    res <- gvaConvergence(fx$ped,
      pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L, kinshipOverrides = badOv
    ),
    "not in the analysis set"
  )
  expect_equal(res$convergence, base$convergence)
})

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# (4) Strict validation propagates: an override above the positive-semidefinite
# bound sqrt(self-kinship product) stops -- applyKinshipOverrides is the strict
# leaf and gvaConvergence must not swallow that error.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
test_that("gvaConvergence errors on an override above the PSD bound", {
  fx <- makeConvFixtureOv()
  # an offspring pair's self-kinship is ~0.5, so the bound is ~0.5; 0.9 exceeds it
  badVal <- data.frame(
    id1 = fx$pop[1], id2 = fx$pop[2], kinship = 0.9,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  expect_error(
    suppressMessages(gvaConvergence(fx$ped,
      pop = fx$pop, nMax = 800L, seed = 11L, kinshipOverrides = badVal
    )),
    "above the maximum"
  )
})

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# (5) reportGV fidelity -- the keep-all / issue-#9 path: an override on a real
# one-unknown-parent rankable animal runs clean and is honored (the
# "N kinship override(s) applied." message fires). On qcPed the convergence
# metrics are gu-free (always 1.0), so the override cannot change the OUTPUT
# curve there; the keep-all NUMERIC is covered by reportGV's tests
# (test_reportGV.R) and test_correctUnknownParentMeanKinship.R, since
# gvaConvergence reuses the identical correctUnknownParentMeanKinship() call and
# returns no per-animal mean kinship of its own.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
test_that("gvaConvergence honors an override on a one-unknown-parent animal", {
  ped <- nprcgenekeepr::qcPed
  X <- "0K7VJN" # male, one-unknown (sire missing) -- see test_reportGV.R
  Y <- "N2XF08" # known parentage
  isU <- function(x) is.na(x) | nprcgenekeepr:::isGeneratedUnknownId(x)
  # fixture guards: fail loudly if qcPed changes instead of mis-testing
  expect_true(all(c(X, Y) %in% as.character(ped$id)))
  expect_true(xor(isU(ped$sire[ped$id == X]), isU(ped$dam[ped$id == X])))

  ov <- data.frame(id1 = X, id2 = Y, kinship = 0.25, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  res <- NULL
  expect_message(
    res <- gvaConvergence(ped,
      nMax = 200L, grid = c(25L, 50L, 100L), seed = 1L, kinshipOverrides = ov
    ),
    "kinship override"
  )
  expect_s3_class(res, "nprcgenekeeprGVConv")

  # qcPed is gu-free -> the override cannot change the (always-1.0) curve; it
  # must still converge at the grid floor exactly as the no-override run does
  base <- gvaConvergence(ped, nMax = 200L, grid = c(25L, 50L, 100L), seed = 1L)
  expect_equal(res$convergence, base$convergence)
})

1261:#### Learning 290 -- **A plan's stated RATIONALE for a load-bearing formula choice can be arithmetically INVERTED -- so before writing a single RED literal, compute EVERY candidate formula on real data, and if the direction contradicts the plan, present the correction with numbers and let the owner ratify (don't parrot the plan's headline OR its reasoning). And a crafted-pedigree RED test only PINS a formula variant if the fixture makes the ratified and rejected forms give DIFFERENT values.** Issue #118 Slice 3 (E3 variance effective size, `calcNeVariance(ped)`) under strict TDD -- exported pure fn reusing S311's `getLivingBreeders()`, additive `neVariance` bundle field, a SECOND "Variance Ne" column in the existing Effective Population Size block; 5 `AskUserQuestion` gates, 0 stakeholder corrections; full suite 3712 pass/0 fail/0 error, lint 0, spelling clean, `devtools::check()` 0/0/0, Phase 3E on real qcPed. **(a) The plan's recommendation AND its rationale were both wrong about DIRECTION -- worked numbers caught it.** The #118 plan (Dragon D-7 / D-d) recommended the "mean-adjusted Crow-Kimura form" *because "the bare `(4N-4)/(Vk+2)` overstates Ne."* Computing all three candidates on the real bundled pedigree (`N=156, kbar=5.28, Vk=16.54`) showed the opposite: **bare = 33.4 (the LOWEST), general Crow-Kimura = 110.9, rescale-to-replacement = 141.7.** The plan's whole headline narrative ("reproductive skew drags E3 far below E2") holds ONLY under the bare form -- which is dimensionally inconsistent here (it plugs a `kbar=5.28`-scale variance into a `kbar=2` formula), so the dramatic low number is an ARTIFACT, not a finding. I presented the three candidates + values + the inversion via `AskUserQuestion`; the owner ratified the general Crow-Kimura form `(N·kbar-1)/(kbar-1+Vk/kbar)` (the standard generalization; reduces to the classic `(4N-2)/(Vk+2)` at replacement) and `N<2 → NA`. Lesson: for a load-bearing formula decision, a worked-numbers gate turns a plan ASSUMPTION into evidence and is where an inverted rationale surfaces -- do it in PRE-RED, before the RED literals depend on it ([[observation-vs-decision]]). This is the S287(b) "run the metric on real data during planning" discipline applied at the IMPLEMENTATION gate. **(b) A crafted RED fixture pins a formula VARIANT only if the two candidate forms DISAGREE on it.** The discriminating test (`discPed`) used `kbar=3 (!=2)`: the ratified general form gives **1.875**, the bare form gives **1.0** -- so a wrong (bare) GREEN implementation FAILS. A `kbar=2` fixture would give the SAME value under both forms (the general form reduces to the bare at replacement), silently passing a bare implementation. Design at least one fixture where the ratified and rejected forms diverge, and VERIFY the exact expected literal by computing the formula directly with the existing helpers (`getLivingBreeders`/`findOffspring`) BEFORE writing it -- RED asserted a hand-verified 1.875/2.5, not a guess. **(c) A deterministic metric can legitimately produce Ne > census -- don't bake a "Ne < N" invariant into a test.** On qcPed the variance Ne (26.41) exceeds both E2 (17.78) AND the census (18 living breeders) because families are more even than Poisson (`Vk<kbar`) -- a real feature of the variance effective size. Computing qcPed's value during RED-DESIGN (not just relying on the plan's example) caught that a planned "expect Ne < N" assertion would have failed; the test instead asserts finite/positive + the exact pinned value 26.405868. **(d) A mid-session "record X for a future session" request = file a scoped tracker item NOW, do NOT start X.** The owner asked mid-work to "place an audit task for another session" (are there citations for each calculation?); the complete job of RECORDING it is one GitHub issue (#120, an AUDIT_WORKSTREAM task with the calculations enumerated) -- filed immediately, then straight back to the E3 gate (FM #2/#13: do the full job of the request without letting it become the session's work). **(e) Additive wiring mechanics (carried from S311, all held):** `neVariance` rides AFTER `neSexRatio` (bundle element #9) -- update BOTH `expect_named` copies (2-space + 4-space, NOT byte-identical, two edits); a SECOND `<th>/<td>` column in the EXISTING Effective Population Size block, not a third block; `1.0` literals (not `1`) for `implicit_integer_linter` (`.lintr` has `indentation_linter=NULL` + `line_length_linter(80)`, and `tests/` is lint-excluded -- so only R/*.R needs ≤80 cols); `Kimura` hand-added to `inst/WORDLIST` sorted (`update_wordlist` NOT run -- Crow/Wright/Fisher already recognized); `document()`'s `@family` cascade re-touched sibling `.Rd` cross-links (verify cross-link-only). (Strict TDD: PRE-RED firsthand reads + real-data computation of all candidate formulas + D-d/degeneracy scope gate → RED (new `test_calcNeVariance.R` + 3 extended, all failing for the right reason, 0 skips under `NOT_CRAN=true`, golden-master `fe`/`fg`/`fgSE`/`neGD`/`neSexRatio`/counts + #9/#73/#76/#2/#86/#82/#13 intact) → GREEN (`calcNeVariance` + bundle + `@return` + both display surfaces + `document()`) → concluded no-refactor per owner; Phase 3E on real qcPed: `neVariance=26.41` rendered beside `neSexRatio=17.78`.)

cat >> PROJECT_LEARNINGS.md <<'EOF'

#### Learning 292 -- **An "unasserted warning" triage starts by REPRODUCING with the full call stack, and the cause can be a test fixture that violates the function's documented contract rather than a production defect; under this project's testthat 2e, `expect_warning(expr, regex)` swallows EVERY warning in `expr`, so a nested `expect_warning(expect_error(...))` also absorbs duplicated warnings; a characterization fix has no honest RED -- say so at the gate.** (S314, issue #121 -- 7 unasserted suite warnings; test-only change, 2 files; 0 stakeholder corrections; 1 scope `AskUserQuestion`-equivalent gate run in prose because the tool was unavailable.) **(a) [triage by reproduction, not by the issue's hypothesis]** #121 attributed the 5 pyramid warnings to "`max()` on an empty/all-NA vector". The failing `max()` was located by running the `testServer` block under `withCallingHandlers()` and printing `sys.calls()` from the handler (testthat's own warning trace stops at shiny's `flushReact` and never reaches the call site): `renderPlot -> getPyramidPlot -> getPedMaxAge -> max(ped$age, na.rm=TRUE)` on a fixture with a `birth` column and NO `age` column (`max(NULL)` -> `-Inf`). `getPyramidPlot()` documents that it needs `sex` + `age`, so the FIXTURE broke the contract; `qcStudbook` output always has `age`, so normal app use never hits it. A probe of four inputs (qcPed / all-NA `age` / zero-row / no `age` column) showed the spurious warning IS reachable in production only on degenerate input (all-NA or empty ages), and even there the plot renders correctly (`-Inf < binWidth` falls into the existing fallback). Fix = give the fixture `age` (mirrors `pyramidTestPed()` in `test_modPyramid_coverage.R`, whose comment already says "renders without warning"); hardening `getPedMaxAge()`/`getPyramidPlot()` was offered as a separate Option B and NOT taken. **(b) [testthat edition]** `DESCRIPTION` has no `Config/testthat/edition`, so the suite runs 2e: `expect_warning(expr, regexp)` captures ALL warnings in `expr` (3e would capture only the first and let the rest bubble). That makes `expect_warning(expect_error(f(), "msg"), "warning regex")` the right shape for an error path that also emits a documented warning -- here `checkKinshipOverrides()`'s "valid only for inbred pairs" (> 0.5) warning, which `gvaConvergence` hits TWICE (`prepareKinshipOverrides` validates, then `applyKinshipOverrides` re-validates); the nested form asserts the documented behavior without coupling to the duplicate count. `expect_no_warning({ ... })` (used in `test_modInput_sexSpecificAge.R`) is the project idiom for "re-render must be warning-free" and wraps the whole `setInputs` sequence inside the `testServer` block. **(c) [RED for test hygiene]** RED = the `expect_no_warning()` wrapper over the unchanged fixture: 1 failure, 0 errors, message `... no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf` (right reason; the other 4 warnings still bubble, which is fine). The gvaConvergence assertion PASSES immediately because it characterizes existing, intended behavior -- there is no honest failing state without bending production code, so I flagged it in the RED report instead of inventing one. **(d) [clean regression read must include `warning`]** S313 noted it; applied: `sum(failed)`, `sum(error)` AND `sum(warning)`. Final full-suite read: failed 0 / error 0 / warning 0 / skipped 167 (matches S313's 167) except 1 env-caused failure (see e). **(e) [environment quirks of this checkout]** renv is NOT restored here: a bare `Rscript` dies bootstrapping renv. Use `NOT_CRAN=true RENV_CONFIG_AUTOLOADER_ENABLED=FALSE Rscript --no-init-file` with `pkgload::load_all(".")` (the user library has every `DESCRIPTION` dep except `devtools`/`rcmdcheck`, so package versions may differ from `renv.lock`). Under `load_all` the package is not INSTALLED, so `test_getVersion.R` fails ("2.0.0 (NA)": `getVersion(date=TRUE)` reads the date via `sessioninfo::package_info("nprcgenekeepr")`) -- environmental, passes under `R CMD check` which installs the package. `R CMD build` has no `--no-init-file` option (warns; harmless). There is no git remote here, so `gh issue list/close` and `git push` are unavailable. **(f) [scratch-dir hygiene]** `/tmp/s314_check` ALREADY held a previous day's tarball/`check.log`/`.Rcheck`; I had assumed it was empty and tried `rm -rf ./*` (blocked by the sandbox). Stale build artifacts would have made `R CMD check nprcgenekeepr_*.tar.gz` silently check an OLD tarball -- so `ls` a scratch dir before reusing it and prefer a fresh `mkdir` with a new name. **(g) [honest deviation]** I told the owner I would "add an `age` column" but REPLACED the unused `birth` column with `age` (the module/`getPyramidPlot` read only `sex`/`age`); the three other `test_modPyramid.R` fixtures (never re-rendered, so inert) still carry `birth` without `age`. Carried as applied: [[observation-vs-decision]] (scope gate before RED; Option A recommended, owner chose), [[consult-project-source-of-truth]] (used the sibling fixture + the `expect_no_warning` precedent), [[check-process-history-before-rerunning-work]].
EOF
tail -c 300 PROJECT_LEARNINGS.md; echo; grep -c '^#### Learning 292' PROJECT_LEARNINGS.md; tail -3 /tmp/s314_check_fresh/check.log
